call_points.text: ₹601 Cr capex adds 66,000 KL a year and close to 10,000 MT of resin capacity.
Decorative volume growth was low single digit; value growth high single digit.
Industrial grew double digits, with project and construction chemicals also double digit.
Industrial price rises of about 5% so far, with another 3-5% expected in Q2.
Q2 will consume high-cost inventory, but price increases should offset it.
Geopolitical conflict, high crude prices and rupee depreciation are key risks.
FY27 margin endeavour stays at 13-14%, the historical band; FY26 was said to be in that range.
Auto customers have granted price increases effective from a date, though quantum was not disclosed.
Decorative grew mid-single digit or lower in Q4; industrial slightly higher single digit, with auto near double digit.
Industrial powder and liquid coating capacity utilisation is 70-75%, with sufficient headroom.
Capex is described as more or less normal and in line with previous years.
Decorative projects are about 10% plus of sales; new businesses also 10% plus, slightly higher.
Board recommended a dividend of 250%, ₹2.5 per share, for FY26.
West Asia crisis, crude surge and rupee depreciation named as key risks; demand visibility is wait-and-watch.
Other expenses fell ~150 bps YoY as a percentage of sales on fixed-cost leverage and spend efficiency, not a Q4 truing-up.
Management sees five months of improving trend across verticals as green shoots, but will not forecast full-year industry growth.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A demand was raised during the financial year 2022-23 on account of discrepancy between Input Tax Credit (“ITC”) claimed by the Company in GSTR 3B and data appearing in GSTR 2A for FY 2017-18. FY 2017-18 was the first year of implementation of GST, the data fetched in GSTR 2A on GST portal was not accurate and complete. The Company has relevant records to prove its claim for ITC.
tax_litigation.status: The Company on 5th March 2025 had informed the Stock Exchanges that an Order had been received from the Joint Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai, giving partial relief in respect of the appeal filed against the said demand. The demand has been reduced to Rs. 15.16 Crores. The Company has relevant records to prove its claim and shall file a further appeal against the said Order before the GST Tribunal. The current status of the litigation remains same as disclosed in the previous quarter ended 31st December, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Order under Section 73(9) of Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 has been received showing demand on account of alleged short payment of GST on the turnover declared in GSTR-9 and wrong availment of Input Tax Credit for FY 2018-19 for the State of New Delhi. The Order has been passed based on wrong understanding of the facts and records and is an error apparent on the face of the record. The Company has already paid adequate and appropriate taxes, as required, and the same is reflected in the GST returns filed during FY 2018-19. The Company has relevant records to prove its claims. The Company is in the process of filing application for rectification of order/appeal.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal and personal hearing is awaited. The current status of the litigation remains same as disclosed in the previous quarter ended 31st December, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has filed an appeal against the Order under Section 73(9) Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 issued for the state of Maharashtra for partial disallowance of Input Tax Credit ("ITC") and alleged short payment of tax on some supplies during the FY 2020-21. The Order has been passed based on wrong understanding of the facts/records/law and there are apparent errors in the Order. The Company has already paid adequate and appropriate taxes, as required by the law. The Company has also filed an application for rectification of the Order.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal and personal hearing is awaited. The current status of the litigation remains same as disclosed in the previous quarter ended 31st December, 2025.

guidance.statement: Endeavour to maintain EBITDA margin at 13-14% for FY27.
Midterm endeavour to reach 14%-plus EBITDA margin.
Industrial price increases of another 3-5% expected in Q2FY27.

operating_notes.text: Decorative projects contribute about 10% plus of sales and new businesses (waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finishes) also about 10% plus, slightly higher.
Industrial powder and liquid coating capacity utilisation is 70-75%, with sufficient headroom for growth.
Paint-as-a-service is present in more than 250 cities and the painter programme covers more than 1.2 lakh painters.
Decorative volume growth was low single digit and value growth high single digit in Q1FY27.
Industrial price increases of about 5% were taken so far, with another 3-5% expected in Q2FY27.
The ₹601 Cr capex adds 66,000 KL a year and close to 10,000 MT of resin capacity over 2-plus years.

timeline.summary: On its 6 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Kansai Nerolac said consolidated Q4 revenue rose 7.5% and PBDIT 30.6%, reiterated a 13-14% FY27 margin endeavour and detailed four decorative price hikes totalling a higher single-digit increase.

On 3 August 2026, Kansai Nerolac's Q1FY27 call disclosed a ₹601 Cr capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur, adding 66,000 KL a year and close to 10,000 MT of resin capacity over 2-plus years.
